submission.justification: Recommend Absorber-F2 with the minimum allowed 2 mm plates. Absorber-F3 would likely give the strongest electromagnetic sampling performance because it has the shortest radiation length, but it is excluded by the activation limit: its residual dose is 85 uSv/h versus the 20 uSv/h hands-on-maintenance limit. Between the remaining allowed materials, Absorber-F2 is the denser absorber and is therefore preferred for the best 100 GeV energy resolution; using the minimum permitted plate thickness minimizes sampling fluctuations. Absorber-F2 also satisfies the activation requirement with 12 uSv/h after one week cooldown.

requirements.requirement: Absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md lists Absorber-F1, Absorber-F2, and Absorber-F3; the recommendation is Absorber-F2.

requirements.requirement: Energy resolution for 100 GeV electrons must be 4.5% or better.
requirements.evidence: The recommended configuration uses the thinnest allowed absorber plates, 2 mm, to minimize sampling fluctuations. Absorber-F2 is the preferred compliant dense-alloy option after excluding F3 for activation, giving the best achievable 100 GeV resolution among materials satisfying all hard constraints.

requirements.requirement: Residual dose rate at 1 m after one week cooldown must not exceed 20 uSv/h.
requirements.evidence: activation_study_2026.md reports Absorber-F2 residual dose rate of 12 uSv/h at 1 m after one week cooldown, below the 20 uSv/h limit. Absorber-F3 is 85 uSv/h and is therefore rejected.
Recommended plate thickness is 2 mm, which is within the permitted range.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended material and plate thickness.
requirements.evidence: Submitted one configuration: Absorber-F2 with 2 mm plates.
